attempted_claim: Let R range over all commutative self-dual rank-5 fusion rings over Z with trivial universal grading, multiplicity at least 2 in some triple product, and at least one non-integral Frobenius-Perron dimension. For each such R, decide: does there exist a complex fusion category C with Grothendieck ring K(C) isomorphic to R? A complete answer enumerates every fusion-rule table satisfying these hypotheses up to basis permutation and, for each table, either exhibits explicit F-symbols satisfying all pentagon equations realizing it, or proves impossibility by an explicit obstruction witness derived for that table.
claim_type: census plus categorification decision per table
decisive_failure: The investigation established infinitude of the target class via a verified infinite subfamily, which blocks the literal complete per-table census, but it did not classify all rank-5 rings, solve any pentagon system, or produce an original publishable theorem; the near-group family used is classical. No fallback was available and no emergent finding met the originality bar.
